bacteria: Hovanec & DeLong 1996, Appl. Environ. Microbiol. 62(8): nitrifier succession in new aquaria takes weeks, so a fishless cycle runs 2 to 6 weeks
Growth, die-off and conversion rates are tuned to that cycle length and are a game abstraction, not measurements
nitrite: Lewis & Morris 1986, Toxicity of nitrite to fish: a review, Trans. Am. Fish. Soc. 115(2)
Per-species tolerance is chemistry.nitriteTolerance in content/species/*.json
nitrate: Camargo, Alonso & Salamanca 2005, Nitrate toxicity to aquatic animals, Chemosphere 58(9)
The yield scales game nitrate into the range a hobby test kit reads
ph: Wurts & Durborow 1992, Interactions of pH, carbon dioxide, alkalinity and hardness in fish ponds, SRAC 464: nitrification consumes alkalinity and lowers pH where the buffer is weak
Biome targets are typical hobby values for each water type

Blackwater: wild Rio Negro water is about pH 4 to 5 with almost no carbonate hardness (Küchler, Miekeley & Forsberg 2000, J. Braz. Chem. Soc. 11(3), A contribution to the chemical characterization of rivers in the Rio Negro Basin, Brazil; Furch 1984 in Sioli (ed.), The Amazon, Junk)

The blackwater target of 6.0 is a deliberate hobby-practice value set above the wild figures: the species are kept and bred at pH 5.5 to 6.5 (SeriouslyFish profiles for Paracheirodon axelrodi and Apistogramma hongsloi), and it keeps nitrate acidification above the 5.5 floor used for the weakest species
CO2 is not offered in blackwater: with KH about 1 there is almost no carbonate buffer, so injected CO2 would crash the pH (same SRAC 464 reasoning)
kh: Wurts & Durborow 1992, SRAC 464: nitrification consumes about 7 mg alkalinity as CaCO3 per mg ammonia-N
sourceWater is a typical mains-water carbonate hardness for fresh biomes and a typical salt-mix hardness for marine and brackish ones
temperature: Newton's law of cooling toward room temperature; a thermostat heater holds the setpoint that suits the stocked fish (their shared comfort range, else the biome target), and one tier is strong enough to reach 31 C in a 21 C room; every tier reaches the same setpoint, but a higher tier closes the gap faster while warming up (game abstraction)
Biome targets are typical hobby values (reef 24 to 27 C)
salinity: Seawater is about 35 ppt; brackish mangrove tanks are kept at about 10 to 20 ppt
Drift stands in for evaporation and top-up
equipment: Game abstraction. Algae growth follows light energy: a lamp at the default intensity 0.8 on a 12 h schedule keeps the baseline rate, stronger lamps and longer photoperiods grow more algae, and a dark tank grows none
Injected CO2 lowers pH and, by feeding plants, leaves algae less to grow on (Wurts & Durborow 1992, SRAC 464 for the CO2-pH link); flow from a wave maker discourages algae settling
stress: Game abstraction: out-of-range pH, temperature, salinity and hardness stunt growth and slowly harm fish, far more gently than ammonia or starvation
